summary: Feed s180_triple to SIEM is degraded: 15.3% oversize frames (up to 8108B) dropped by 1518B SIEM NIC, 19.4% duplicates wasting capacity, and 28.3% ERSPAN-encapsulated traffic not parsed. Broker-side slicing, deduplication and ERSPAN stripping required.

findings.root_cause: 581 of 3808 frames (15.3%) exceed SIEM 1G port MTU of 1518 bytes, largest 8108 bytes. Likely jumbo frames plus ERSPAN overhead forwarded unchanged by packet broker.
findings.impact_on_tool: SIEM NIC silently drops oversize frames, creating 15.3% blind spot; events/flows incomplete and detection coverage reduced despite SIEM not needing full payload.

recommended_fix.why: Tool needs_full_payload=false, so broker can trim/slice frames to 1518 bytes to fit tool MTU while preserving headers for SIEM detection, preventing NIC drops.

findings.root_cause: 19.4% duplicates (737/3808) indicates overlapping SPAN/ERSPAN sources aggregated on broker without deduplication.
findings.impact_on_tool: Wastes SIEM ingest, storage and license, inflates event counts and can skew correlation/analytics and obscure true traffic volume.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet-broker deduplication to remove duplicate packets before delivery to SIEM, restoring accurate counts without losing unique traffic.

findings.root_cause: 28.3% of frames (1076/3808) arrive inside ERSPAN tunnel; broker is forwarding encapsulated traffic without stripping.
findings.impact_on_tool: SIEM without tunnel decapsulation cannot parse inner headers/flows, missing over a quarter of traffic for detection and correlation.

recommended_fix.why: Strip ERSPAN headers on the packet broker to deliver native inner packets the SIEM can natively parse and analyze.
